clinical_knowledge.topic: Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management emphasizes Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: anterolateral shoulder pain worsening with overhead reaching and sleeping on that side

Key HPI features: 50M painter reports 3 months of aching pain in his right shoulder. Pain worsens when painting ceilings, reaching overhead, or sleeping directly on the right shoulder. Denies any sudden fall or injury.
Objective/Exam findings: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Rotator cuff tear without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Progressive symptoms without trauma suggest overuse tendinopathy rather than acute tear.
management_principles: Evidence-based diagnostic and therapeutic protocol for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome
: Perform Neer and Hawkins impingement tests
Recommend physical therapy for rotator cuff strengthening and scapular stabilization
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.subjective: Patient presenting with symptoms of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome. anterolateral shoulder pain worsening with overhead reaching and sleeping on that side. 50M painter reports 3 months of aching pain in his right shoulder. Pain worsens when painting ceilings, reaching overhead, or sleeping directly on the right shoulder. Denies any sudden fall or injury.
reference_soap.objective: Complete vital signs and focused physical examination required. Diagnostic workup tailored for Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
reference_soap.assessment: Clinical presentation highly suggestive of Rotator Cuff Tendinopathy / Subacromial Impingement Syndrome.
reference_soap.plan: After focused examination, begin activity modification and physical therapy for rotator-cuff and scapular strengthening. Consider analgesia only after reviewing contraindications; a subacromial corticosteroid injection can be considered after assessment if symptoms persist. Obtain imaging or refer if there is traumatic onset, objective or progressive weakness, marked loss of passive motion, systemic symptoms, or failure of conservative care.

teaching.diagnosis: Rotator cuff tendinopathy / subacromial impingement syndrome
teaching.one_liner: 50M painter with 3 months of shoulder pain worsening with overhead reaching and sleeping on that side.
red_flags: Acute trauma, objective or progressive weakness, fever, or an acutely hot swollen joint warrants prompt reassessment for another diagnosis

must_ask.objective: Characterize the activities that worsen pain
must_ask.say: Does overhead work like painting ceilings make the pain worse?

must_ask.objective: Ask about night pain when lying on the shoulder
must_ask.say: Does the pain wake you when you sleep on that side?
Was there any specific fall or injury, or has this come on gradually?
How much overhead work does your painting job require daily?

must_ask.objective: Explain physical therapy and injection options
must_ask.say: If the examination supports tendinopathy, we can start physical therapy and discuss an injection only if appropriate after reviewing the risks and alternatives.
